steering_ledger.verbatim: We've ingested multiple EXL3-related research docs. I really want us to build up to a viable path forward for getting this quant working in our project (CPU and MI210) so we can tap into the same performance improvements other people are obtaining on thei nvidia cards.
remember that we are NEVER scared to build custom kernels ourselves!
i'd be more than happy if we become the first people to get this working on this hardware architecture

contradiction_pass.intake-1528: The author’s own post says prefill up to +20%, while figure caption ranges imply roughly +51–60%; quality chart compares 256 EXL3 experts to 168 W4A16 experts. Bounded exact-claim search found no independent H200 reproduction (provisional).
contradiction_pass.intake-1529: README excludes MI210 gfx90a and requires ROCm >=7.2.4; its direct validation is on gfx1151, so no evidence for MI210 (repository scope check; not a contradiction to RDNA support).
contradiction_pass.intake-1533: Current docs support an AVX CPU MoE expert path, but the use case is CPU offload/CPU-tail within ExLlamaV3; optimized eligibility is mul1-specific, so MCG/general CPU-only support is not established.

dive_recommendations.settle: Kernel inventory, WMMA-to-MFMA port scope, ROCm 6.2 versus 7.2.4 dependency, correctness harness and whether a custom MI210 implementation can be isolated.

dive_recommendations.reason: Concrete current CPU trellis expert kernels directly inform the requested CPU path.
dive_recommendations.settle: Actual kernel math/layout and codebook/tensor limits; what can be adapted into a CPU backend or GGUF/ggml operator, and which EPYC Zen 5 instructions apply.

dive_recommendations.reason: Primary performance report motivating the work; attached figures were recovered and inspected.
dive_recommendations.settle: Exact model/checkpoint/configuration, benchmark protocol, chart-vs-post discrepancy, reproducibility inputs and when promised source/report appears.

dive_recommendations.reason: A recent custom CUDA implementation may expose algorithm/test patterns even though it targets Blackwell.
dive_recommendations.settle: Which trellis decode and correctness structures are portable as specifications, and which gains are architecture/runtime-specific.

dive_recommendations.reason: Marlin is the unpack/GEMM comparator named by the Hopper post.

dive_recommendations.reason: The checkpoint illustrates current EXL3/TR3 quality measurement and mixed-K loader requirements.
dive_recommendations.settle: What its reproducibility bundle actually proves and whether any smaller checkpoint is suitable for a project-side correctness fixture.
